Nope... check 7060.7(B)

tl;dr: Ellis act does not preempt local land use regulation.

The Ellis Act was written to implement the property owner's supposed constitutional right to withdraw from a regulated market. So the City can't refuse a demolition permit, but it still can attach regulations to how it would be done. That's why I put on the sewer capping/etc. in my comment. Other land use regulations that would govern the new construction (if any) on the vacant parcels are unaffected by the Ellis Act. There was a infamous case that came out of the (People's Republic) of Santa Monica where an obnoxious owner of high rise apartments hated the rent controls and decided to leave his residential tower vacant rather than cow-tow to the rent control board. The City Atty was powerless to force the owner to actually use the building so the City decided to adopt a fire sprinkler ordinance. It only applied to new construction and to any building that had been "vacant for more than one year". The retrofit costs on that stubborn owner were in the Millions.
